[00:00:03] Ben (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the weekly POC sync for NovaMed. We got about 45 minutes on the calendar. Quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Alex (NovaMed): Hi Ben, Alex here. Jordan and Sam are with me.
[00:00:18] Jordan (NovaMed): Jordan on the call.
[00:00:20] Sam (NovaMed): Sam here.
[00:00:23] Priya (Redwood): Priya from Redwood SE, hey all. Miguel will drop in if needed.
[00:00:30] Ben: Great. Quick agenda: onboarding progress, access setup, environment readiness, review of the small benchmark Priya ran last week, then next steps and security items. Anything to add?
[00:00:40] Alex: Sounds good. We also want to surface infra blockers, if any.
[00:00:45] Ben: Cool. Priya, do you want to start with the benchmark recap?
[00:00:50] Priya: Sure — so I ran a smoke suite against the hosted endpoint and the dedicated test pool we spun up. High level — hosted latencies were stable around 220-280ms p95 on the short prompts, dedicated pool we saw p95 of 120-150ms but throughput is what matters, we hit about 45 rps with batching at 4 requests per batch. There was some K-V cash miss rate — excuse me — KV cache miss rate on the long prompt path which increased token generation time by ~30%.
[00:01:25] Jordan: When you say KV cash, you mean the KV cache for autoregressive context? We worry about warm vs cold.
[00:01:30] Priya: Yes. The cache warm-up is important; our runtime does prefix caching but because your prompt templates include long medical notes, the split between unique prefixes and repeated headers is bigger so cache hit rate is lower. We recommended a small prompt refactor to move repeating patient metadata into a preface token that can be cached.
[00:01:50] Alex: Okay, that matches our expectations. We're also planning to chunk long notes anyway.
[00:01:55] Priya: Good. On tuning, we tried 4-bit quantization on the dedicated instance image — transcription notes: quantizashun — and saw a 1.8x throughput improvement but slight increase in hallucination on a couple of edge prompts. We'll share the eval matrix.
[00:02:15] Sam: Is 4-bit quant safe for PHI? Our security policy requires validated parity tests and bitflip protections.
[00:02:22] Priya: Totally — quantization itself doesn't change the encryption at rest or in transit. But we need to validate quality on your audit prompts. We'll run some regression tests and include the outputs for your audit.
[00:02:34] Ben: On the access side, Tasha, were you able to set up the cross-account role for Redwood to pull test objects from S3?
[00:02:41] Tasha: Almost — I created the role but I need the exact ARN for the Redwood test runner. I posted a note in the shared doc. I can finish it today if Ben sends the IPs and ARN pattern.
[00:02:52] Ben: I'll send the IP list and the role ARN template in the notes after the call.
[00:02:56] Miguel (Redwood, off): quick note — we also added a temporary API key with limited scope for the test harness.
[00:03:02] Alex: Great. About network — we need clarity on VPC peering or private link. Which do you recommend?
[00:03:08] Priya: For NovaMed's size and PHI, VPC peering with private IPs is simplest if you're hosting in the same cloud region. If you need cross-region or a managed option, PrivateLink gives more controlled endpoint management. We'll map both options in the architecture doc.
[00:03:25] Sam: We need to ensure logs contain user_id, request_id, model_version and redaction flags. Can you confirm Redwood's audit logs include those fields?
[00:03:33] Ben: Yes, our console emits per-request metadata. We'll share an example log and the retention settings. Note: retention beyond 90 days is an add-on.
[00:03:42] Sam: Also, do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[00:03:45] Priya: Yes — the private deployment path supports CMK via KMS and HSM integrations. For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer KMS in a few regions; we'll confirm which regions for your account.
[00:03:58] Jordan: On testing infra, last week we had a failure where the Dedicated pool autoscaler throttled the job. Has that been addressed?
[00:04:05] Priya: We adjusted the autoscale policy and increased the reserved headroom for your test tenant; that prevented the throttle in our reruns. We'll share the autoscale config that we used.
[00:04:15] Alex: Perfect. For the benchmark shared earlier, can we get raw logs and the exact prompt set so our data team can re-run?
[00:04:20] Priya: Yup — link to raw logs and a reproducible harness will be in the /shared/poc folder. Expect a link after I upload.
[00:04:27] Ben: Quick note: next week we want to try a longer-run 50k token throughput test to see how KV cache behaves over time with rolling sessions. Priya will own that.
[00:04:35] Priya: I'll do it. It may run a couple hours; I'll provide the summary and tail-latency graphs.
[00:04:40] Sam: For the security deep dive, can we get a redwood contact for SOC2 artifacts and penetration testing reports?
[00:04:45] Ben: I'll include the security contact in the invite for the follow-up; we can share SOC2 report and recent pentest summary under NDA.
[00:04:52] Alex: About evaluation — we noticed a few hallucination cases with medication names. Is there a recommended mitigation besides prompt engineering?
[00:05:00] Priya: We can try constrained decoding (higher logit bias for known tokens), stronger system prompts, and, importantly, reranking by a light-weight model for critical outputs. Also, model variant choice matters — sometimes switching to a larger precision model helps for factuality. We'll include options in the eval report.
[00:05:18] Jordan: Any blockers from Redwood's side for the POC timeline? We're aiming to complete pilot evals by end of month.
[00:05:24] Ben: No blockers on our side — just need the sample data, S3 role, and to confirm security call. We'll push the bench runs as soon as Priya has the sample.
[00:05:31] Miguel: Quick FYI — pricing for Dedicated varies by region and committed hours; Ben will follow up with the quote.
[00:05:38] Ben: Yep.
[00:05:40] Alex: We have one compliance nuance: NovaMed requires data residency in us-east-1 for PHI. Any constraints?
[00:05:45] Priya: We have dedicated pools in us-east-1, and Private deploy is an option if you need on-prem. For hosted, we'll ensure the env pins to us-east-1. We'll document the SLA differences.
[00:05:56] Sam: Also, for logs we need the ability to turn off storing prompts at rest for some datasets. Is that configurable?
[00:06:01] Ben: Yes — we can set retention to zero for certain buckets and disable prompt logging for specific routes. We'll show the console toggle.
[00:06:08] Alex: Awesome. Anything else on onboarding?
[00:06:11] Tasha: Small infra note — our security team wants the Redwood test runner IPs allowed to the S3 endpoint and the test harness to use a jumpbox. I left details in the shared doc.
[00:06:20] Ben: We'll review that after.
[00:06:22] Priya: One more tech note — we noticed tokenization differences between your internal tokenizer and the model's tokenizer on a couple of clinical shorthand terms. This affects token counts and billing. Recommend normalizing tokenization or pre-tokenizing in your pipeline.
[00:06:36] Jordan: Good call; we'll add a preprocess step.
[00:06:40] Ben: Alright, quick recap of concrete next steps and owners — Alex will upload sample, Tasha will finalize role + firewall, Priya will run 50k token bench and KV cache profiling, Ben will send pricing and security contacts, Sam will gather SOC2 questions. We'll schedule the security deep-dive for week of 8/24.
[00:06:58] Alex: That works.
[00:07:00] Ben: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links. End call.
[00:07:05] (meeting ends)
